DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Cell Carcinoma.

The combination of gross hematuria, right flank pain, a history of recurrent UTIs, and the definitive exclusion of kidney stones on non-contrast CT strongly points to a renal mass. While the CT was normal, this specific clinical picture is the classic presentation for renal cell carcinoma, which can sometimes be subtle or require a contrast-enhanced scan for definitive visualization.
